objective: Provide a bounded AI-native userspace supervisor for persistent agent execution, durable objectives, event-driven dispatch, checkpoint and recovery, secure tools and messages, anomaly quarantine, and M240 adaptive budget integration while keeping model inference and high-level reasoning outside kernel authority.

sources.finding: Durable execution depends on event history, deterministic replay, version compatibility, and isolating nondeterministic activities such as LLM calls and external tools from deterministic workflow orchestration.
sources.impact: M241 persists tamper-evident supervisor events and binds recovery to checkpoint digests; model/tool execution remains outside the kernel and is represented as untrusted input.

sources.finding: Priority and preemption require administrator-controlled policy and resource-quota limits because malicious workloads can request excessive priority; non-preempting priority is a supported alternative.
sources.impact: M241 requires policy-verified objective priority and combines it with M240 budgets and authority; agent-provided priority is never execution authority.

sources.finding: Modern agent runtimes separate agent loops, tools, handoffs, sessions, guardrails, resumable state, and tracing.
sources.impact: M241 supplies provider-neutral lifecycle, tool, message, checkpoint, event, and anomaly primitives without embedding a provider-specific model loop.

sources.finding: Input, output, and tool guardrails can block execution with tripwires; tool guardrails run around tool calls, while handoffs have separate semantics.
sources.impact: M241 treats tool requests and agent messages as capability- and authority-gated events and adds supervisor-level anomaly quarantine and generation invalidation.

features: persistent agent registration with tenant, generation, capability mask, trust, and identity binding
durable objective admission with trace, task/session/world/model generation, deadline, priority, provenance, and M240 budget binding
append-only fixed-format SHA-256 chained event journal
replay projection with strict sequence, payload digest, previous digest, and event digest checks
checkpoint digest binding for working, memory, world, and budget state
checkpoint-first recovery with generation and deadline fencing
evidence-bound anomaly recording with agent quarantine, objective quarantine, and generation invalidation
transactional rollback around budget admission, dispatch, checkpoint, recovery, and terminal transitions
bounded in-memory capacities with explicit scale measurements

scale_benchmark.scope: durable userspace admit-dispatch-complete lifecycle including SHA-256 journal events and M240 admission; not model inference or physical accelerator throughput

qualification_limits: M241 is a bounded userspace supervisor contract and does not itself run LLM inference, execute tools, grant OS capabilities, program hardware, migrate processes, or provide a distributed consensus service.

The current implementation has bounded arrays of FAR_MAX_AGENTS=128, FAR_MAX_OBJECTIVES=512, and FAR_MAX_TOOL_REQUESTS=512; thousands or millions of agents require sharding, durable external storage, and independently qualified distributed transport.
Memory integration is digest-bound at the supervisor boundary; it does not replace the existing persistent memory service or claim semantic learning/retraining.
The scale benchmark measures control-plane lifecycle overhead only and does not measure tokens/sec, model latency, accelerator utilization, or energy per inference.
No physical GPU/NPU, HBM/VRAM, IOMMU/DMA, vendor driver, production KMS/PKI, independent builder, or external security review was available.

Production release remains blocked by independent builder, operator signing, physical accelerator, external security review, production PKI/KMS, live multihost migration/rollback, and operator-owned CVE evidence.
